Anthropic.why: Anthropic lists claude-opus-5.5 under two tags: the base anthropic endpoint at the model's list price and a dearer anthropic/fast throughput tier, double the price. Pinned to anthropic: fast is a distinct tier, not a price twin, so 'cheapest' cannot apply.

BaseTen.why: BaseTen lists one deepseek-v4.1-flash offering twice under baseten/fp8 - the global endpoint the account reaches and a dearer US in-region twin (cache read 0.007 against 0.03 per million) - alike in everything else but a 1-token max_completion_tokens listing artifact (32767 against 32768), recorded here as ignored. baseten/fast is a separate tier under its own tag, excluded by the pin. Pinned to baseten/fp8 and taking the cheaper: the keys reach only the global data region, so the cheap-read twin is the one the account is billed by.

DeepInfra.why: DeepInfra lists one deepseek-v4.1-flash offering twice under deepinfra/fp8 at two prices - fresh 0.14, output 0.42, cache read 0.0042 per million (30% off) against fresh 0.3, output 1.2, cache read 0.006 with no discount - alike in quantization (fp8), context length (1048576), max_completion_tokens (131072) and every other identity field the listing carries, so nothing needs ignoring. Taking the cheaper: it prices lowest on the cheapest rule's first key (cache read), and every rise of the cheap row is reported as a possible twin switch.

Alibaba.why: Alibaba lists glm-5.3 under two tags: the base alibaba endpoint at the model's list price and a dearer alibaba/fast throughput tier. Pinned to alibaba: fast is a distinct tier, not a price twin, so 'cheapest' cannot apply.

BaseTen.why: BaseTen lists glm-5.3 under baseten/fp4 at the model's list price beside a dearer baseten/fast throughput tier. Pinned to baseten/fp4: fast is a distinct tier, not a price twin, so 'cheapest' cannot apply.

Mistral.why: Mistral lists glm-5.3 under mistral/zdr and mistral/nvfp4, and nvfp4 itself lists at two prices. Pinned to the single mistral/zdr endpoint at the model's list price: a tag pin must name one tag, and nvfp4 alone would leave the host ambiguous.

Reka.why: Reka lists glm-5.3 under two tags: the base reka endpoint the row has always tracked (its history is this endpoint's own log series, currently 0.17/3.0 with 0.169 cache read) and a reka/fast tier (1M context, 35% off) that is dearer on input but cheaper on output and cache read. Pinned to reka: fast is a distinct tier, not a price twin, so 'cheapest' cannot apply.
